core_obligations: Unwind the definition of eta_f on a complex of f-torsion free modules, applied twice: first to M^bullet with respect to g and then to the result with respect to f (statement span).
Identify the localization in which the two sides are compared as M^i_{fg}, using the canonical identification (M^i_g)_f = M^i_{fg} (proof lines 27846-27847).
Show that in each degree the submodule produced by eta_f eta_g agrees with the submodule produced by eta_fg; the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 27847-27848).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, nonzerodivisors f and g in A, and a complex M^bullet of A-modules such that fg is a nonzerodivisor on every M^i, and asserts the identity eta_f eta_g M^bullet = eta_fg M^bullet (source lines 27839-27844). The second application of eta is to the already-transformed complex, so the two sides live in different localizations, and the proof must say in what sense the identity is meant: objectwise, the statement is that in each degree i the two constructions yield the same submodule of M^i_{fg} = (M^i_g)_f (proof lines 27846-27848). That comparison of submodules under the identification of the two-fold localization is the content of the lemma, and the author leaves the details to the reader.
